claim_en: NO BEFORE AND AFTER, AND THE EPOCH TABLE. The first month after the book's second month (1:1): the chronological rule derived here, Rebbi's Exod 16:35 beside; the eleven months at Sinai in disparagement (the Hebrew; the shelf's English 'praise'); the eras a run is dated by — the exodus, the entry, the Temple built, destroyed, the kings — months as years.
middah: plain (no before and after — the chronological rule stated from 9:1 against 1:1, Rebbi's second exemplar beside; the epoch table stated from the verse's own 'second year of their going out'; the disparagement reading)

claim_en: THE APPOINTED TIME. The first Passover overrides the Sabbath by the verbal analogy with the daily offering's 'in its appointed time' (Num 28:2), and communal impurity by the second 'in its appointed time' (the red-heifer a-fortiori refuted by the second Passover); 'statutes' = the mitzvot on its body, 'ordinances' = the attendant; Onkelos 'what is fitting for it'.
middah: I2 (the verbal analogy 'in its appointed time' with the daily offering's Num 28:2 — the Sabbath override; the a-fortiori from the red heifer refuted by the second Passover, I1, beside; the body/attendant taxonomy plain; the received translation's 'what is fitting for it', ink)

claim_en: THE TELLING BEFORE THE DOING. Keep the Passover in its time so all the festivals fall in season (Deut 16:1); heard at Sinai, told, repeated before performance — three passes over one law; Moses instituted asking and expounding the festival's laws before the festival.
middah: plain (the three passes and the pre-festival exposition stated from the redundancy of 9:4 beside Lev 23:44)

claim_en: THE ONE PASSOVER OF THE WILDERNESS. In disparagement — the only Passover in forty years (Amos 5:25); R. Shimon b. Yochai: the tribe of Levi alone sacrificed, kept the covenant, circumcised; 'as the LORD commanded' the praise; Onkelos names the month Nisan.
middah: plain (the one-Passover reading with R. Shimon b. Yochai's Levi arm as a recorded dispute; the received translation's Nisan for 'the first', ink)

claim_en: THE MEN AND THE HALT. Who they were — a three-arm dispute (Joseph's bearers / Mishael and Eltzafan / a met mitzvah's seventh day); before Aaron then Moses, or the study house; the affected party asks; the men's a-fortiori from the sin offering (blood on the unclean, flesh to the clean) refused by 'I have not heard'; R. Chidka: the sprinkling was the question; merit through the meritorious. Onkelos: 'WAIT' for 'stand', 'prevented', corpse impurity named.
middah: I1 (the men's a-fortiori from the sin offering to the Passover, recorded and REFUSED by the halt — 'I have not heard'; the identity dispute and the inversion plain; the received translation's 'wait' and 'prevented', ink)

claim_en: THE OUTPUT WIDER THAN THE QUESTION; THE DISTANCE PARAMETER. Corpse-impurity was asked, the distant way was not; every impurity by binyan av from the two; 'distant' — R. Akiva and the sages: Modi'im (fifteen mil), R. Eliezer: outside the place of eating (the tithe's analogy), R. Yehuda: outside the court; Onkelos fills 'soul' to corpse impurity.
middah: I3 (the binyan av from the two verses — the corpse-unclean and the distant — to every impurity; R. Eliezer's and R. Yehuda's verbal analogies with the tithe's 'distant', I2, beside; the sages' Modi'im measure a data row; the received translation, ink)

claim_en: THE DOTTED HEH. The upper dot on the heh of 'distant' — the second Passover even for the non-distant who did not keep the first; the Torah's dotted places listed (Gen 16:5, 18:9, 19:33, 33:4, 37:12; Num 3:39, 9:10, 21:30, the second issaron at 29:15; Deut 29:28) — machine-verified: eleven tokens at ten verses carry the mark.
middah: ink (the upper dot on the heh of 'distant' at 9:10 — the mark's own signal, machine-checked; the list of the Torah's dotted places verified at eleven tokens on ten verses)

check.note: the upper dot (U+05C4) on the heh of rechoqa — the token's own accented form carries the mark

claim_en: THE SECOND PASSOVER'S SCOPE. The date and the lamb = the body mitzvot; matzah and bitter herbs = the attendant; no leftover and no bone superadded; 'according to all the statute' = the body mitzvot only — the bone left the general to teach on it — not the seven days' matzah nor the leaven's burning; Onkelos 'the decree of the Passover'.
middah: I8 (the particular that left the general to teach on the general — 'a bone' bounds 'all the statute' to the mitzvot on its body; Issi b. Akavya's 'offer IT' beside; the received translation's 'decree', ink)

claim_en: INDIVIDUALS, NOT THE CONGREGATION; THE KARET FORK. Individuals keep the second (from 'men', 9:6; R. Natan from 'the man'); 'refrained' = could and did not, the sages' Modi'im measure; deliberate; Rebbi: karet for the first and the second, R. Natan: the first alone; the second overrides the Sabbath not impurity; a man not a minor, the woman from 'soul'. Onkelos: one root for 'held back' and 'refrained', 'receive his debt'.
middah: plain (individuals from the narrative's 'men' and R. Natan's 'the man'; the karet fork Rebbi against R. Natan a recorded dispute; the Sabbath override and the impurity refusal stated; the received translation's shared root and 'receive his debt', ink)

claim_en: THE PROSELYTE'S TWO CLAUSES. Not at once — as the native on the fourteenth; converted between the Passovers — R. Shimon b. Elazar excludes him from the second; 'according to the statute' equates him for the Passover, 'one statute... of the land' for all the Torah's mitzvot. Onkelos: 'becomes a proselyte', 'one covenant', 'the established one'.
middah: plain (the native's date for the proselyte and R. Shimon b. Elazar's exclusion read off 'for the proselyte and the native'; 'one statute' widened to the whole Torah; the received translation's conversion verb and 'one covenant', ink)

claim_en: THE CLOUD BY THE WORD; DAYS = A YEAR. 'By the mouth of the LORD' rendered by the Word (the Memra) four times in 9:18-23 — the same phrase as the halt's 'by the mouth of the LORD' at Lev 24:12; the march's third duration 'days' read as a period, a year (the counter idiom).
middah: ink (the received translation's Word for 'the mouth of the LORD' and its year for the bare 'days' at 9:22 — the counter idiom)
